atheist

AY-thee-ist -- three syllables, stress on AY. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Atheist is a person who does not believe in a higher power.

As an atheist, Marcus politely bowed his head during the invocation but did not join in the prayer.

Example

When the survey asks about religious belief, one respondent checks the box marked 'atheist,' stating that she does not believe any god or higher power exists.

A person who does not believe in a higher power is an atheist. The word is a neutral, factual label for a position on belief -- it says nothing about a person's character, values, or behavior.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

nonbeliever: A nonbeliever is anyone who does not hold religious belief — the broadest, most neutral umbrella, taking in the undecided as well as the certain. An atheist stands at one definite point under that umbrella: the settled conviction that no higher power exists.

unbeliever: Unbeliever means much the same as nonbeliever but is usually spoken from inside a faith — believers historically called those outside their religion unbelievers. Atheist is the neutral, self-chosen label for someone certain there is no higher power; unbeliever defines a person by the faith they lack.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

believer: a person who holds religious faith

theist: a person who believes a god exists

Where it sits · how firmly the doubt has settled

skeptic → atheist → antitheist

skeptic vs. atheist: Skeptic is milder and broader than atheist -- a skeptic doubts and questions claims, religious or otherwise, while an atheist has settled on a definite position: no higher power exists.

antitheist vs. atheist: Antitheist goes a step further than atheist: an atheist has settled on the conviction that no higher power exists, while an antitheist actively opposes religion, working to argue belief itself out of existence.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-: without, not (Greek)

root — the-: god (Greek theos)

suffix — -ist: one who believes or practices (Greek -istes)

Put it together: Atheist assembles from Greek a- ('without'), theos ('god'), and -ist ('one who') -- literally 'one who is without god.' The word simply describes a person's position on belief: they do not hold that any higher power exists.

Use the root in a new word: theology: Uncle Ray earned a theology degree before deciding he would rather fix boats.

Root Check

Word Choice

Atheist is a neutral, descriptive term -- it states what a person does not believe, nothing more. Use it factually, the way you would 'violinist' or 'vegetarian,' without any tone of praise or blame in either direction.
